summary:
We developed TERRA GABON, a web platform that turns free satellite data from ESA, NASA and Global Forest Watch into clear, actionable information for Gabon’s forestry and mining sectors.

In Gabon, forest concessions and mining permits cover thousands of hectares. Field teams search them blindly for days, at high cost, and nothing is monitored between visits. Satellite data exists but remains unused, and clouds hide most optical images: in our Okondja test area, only 3 of more than 500 were usable.

TERRA GABON addresses this challenge by combining optical and radar imagery (Sentinel-1, NISAR), which sees through clouds. Users draw their area. The platform then detects logging, deforestation, fires and possible illegal gold mining, maps geological indicators, and generates EUDR zero-deforestation reports, all with GPS coordinates.

This matters because teams no longer travel to search, only to verify. Costs drop, problems are caught earlier, and Gabonese timber stays eligible for the European market.
details:
TERRA GABON — Satellite monitoring for Gabon’s forests and mines

Problem: To inspect forest concessions and mining permits spread over thousands of hectares, companies and authorities send field teams that search blindly for days. Missions are costly, so they are rare, and nobody knows what happens between two visits. Meanwhile, free satellite data is available but scattered, technical and largely unused. Cloud cover makes it even harder: in our test area of Okondja, only 3 of more than 500 recent optical images were usable.

Solution: TERRA GABON is a web platform that turns free satellite data from ESA, NASA and Global Forest Watch into clear, actionable information. Users draw or import their area, and the platform:

  • lists all available satellite images and shows them, before and after;
  • uses radar (Sentinel-1, NISAR) to see through clouds;
  • detects logging, deforestation, fires, bare soil and muddy rivers that may signal illegal gold mining;
  • maps geological indicators (clay and iron-oxide indices, faults) for mining exploration;
  • generates an EUDR “zero-deforestation” compliance report for timber exports to Europe.

Target users: forestry operators, mining companies, consulting firms and public agencies.

Impact: teams no longer travel to search, only to verify. Field costs go down, problems are spotted earlier, and Gabonese timber keeps access to the European market.

Status: a working prototype that already queries real satellite catalogues. Next steps: automatic e-mail alerts, a mobile app for field teams, carbon estimates, and partnerships with national institutions such as AGEOS.
